symptom: On Mendix 11.17.0, where mxbuild --serve builds a complete client in every build of a process, `run --local --watch` still copied deployment/web aside every 50 ms during each build and put it back before the next. Nothing failed; the copies were never needed.
cause: The client-source keep (ako/mxcli#2150) decided whether to work from what a build deleted, and 11.17.0 still deletes its client source: it only no longer needs it back. So the keep's own off-switch never fired, and the one part of the loop that can collide with mxbuild on Windows (an open file blocks another process's delete, mendixlabs/mxcli#1342) ran on a version it does nothing for.
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/client_source_keep.go (keepFixedIn, keepNeededFor, dormant, wake), cmd/mxcli/docker/serve_recovery.go (wakeKeep, before both full-build fallbacks), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go (the boot sets dormant)
insight: A workaround that detects its own necessity from a side effect keeps running when upstream fixes the defect without removing the side effect. When the upstream fix is measured, gate on the version, but make the gate reversible by the symptom: a dormant keep that the existing 'bundle lost its pages' check wakes costs one full build if a later release regresses, where a hard version gate would cost one per change for ever. Keep 'dormant' apart from 'off': off also means 'gave way after a collision', and a wake must not undo that. Live check that needs no log line: count the files in the keep's temp directory while the app runs — 0 on 11.17.0, 79 on 11.16.0, same binary, same four changes.
